clusters.name: Data Ingestion and Transformation Strategy
clusters.description: Which ingestion mechanism or transformation ordering turns raw sources into usable ML inputs?

relations.reading: Data Ingestion and Transformation Strategy requires Pipeline Task Orchestration to be decided first
relations.rationale: Preparation pipelines depend on ingestion completion, scheduling, partitioning, synchronization, and replication triggers.

relations.reading: Choices on Data Ingestion and Transformation Strategy affect the outcomes of Model Packaging Format
relations.rationale: Feature availability and offline-to-online replication directly affect whether serving systems can answer real-time prediction requests.

values.label: Extract-transform-load pipeline
values.description: Extract data, stage it, transform it, then load it into final storage.

values.label: Extract-load-transform pipeline
values.description: Extract data, load it before transformation, then transform it in the destination environment.

values.label: Data acquisition and ingestion mechanism
values.description: Acquire ML data from operational sources and move it through push-based, pull-based, or event-driven ingestion into preparation pipelines.

clusters.name: Preparation Pipeline Structure
clusters.description: Which structural approach organizes and iterates data preparation across sources and processing stages?

values.label: Composable transformation pipeline
values.description: Preparation is organized as immutable, reusable transformation stages that can be tested and recombined across data sources and processing steps.

includes.label: Immutable composable transformations
includes.description: Feature preparation implemented as testable, reusable transformation stages rather than mutable processing logic.

values.label: Partitioned parallel pipeline
values.description: Preparation is organized into partitioned processing stages executed in parallel to scale feature and dataset processing.

includes.label: Partitioned parallel preparation pipelines
includes.description: Offline preparation uses partitioned pipelines and parallel execution for scalable feature processing.

values.label: Integrated adaptive preparation pipeline
values.description: Preparation combines composable transformations and scalable parallel execution with feedback from exploration and validation to refine data acquisition or ingestion.

includes.label: Immutable composable transformations
includes.description: Feature preparation implemented as testable, reusable transformation stages rather than mutable processing logic.

includes.label: Partitioned parallel preparation pipelines
includes.description: Offline preparation uses partitioned pipelines and parallel execution for scalable feature processing.

includes.label: Iterative data-ingestion feedback
includes.description: Feed exploration findings back into acquisition and ingestion when additional or different data is needed.

clusters.name: Data Preparation Automation
clusters.description: Which preparation and feature-engineering activities are automated?

values.label: AutoML-assisted preparation pipeline
values.description: Uses generalized AutoML pipeline automation together with automated preprocessing and feature engineering, while not necessarily automating feature selection or training as separate activities.

includes.label: Automated data preprocessing
includes.description: Automation selects cleaning, imputation, encoding, leakage prevention, and related preprocessing decisions.

includes.label: Automated feature engineering
includes.description: Automation generates and selects useful features during pipeline construction.

includes.label: AutoML pipeline automation
includes.description: Automate multiple pipeline activities through generalized search and limited-code model development.

values.label: End-to-end automated ML pipeline
values.description: Automates the full preparation and modeling workflow, including preprocessing, feature engineering and selection, pipeline automation, internally scripted activities, and model training.

includes.label: Automated data preprocessing
includes.description: Automation selects cleaning, imputation, encoding, leakage prevention, and related preprocessing decisions.

includes.label: Automated feature engineering
includes.description: Automation generates and selects useful features during pipeline construction.

includes.label: AutoML pipeline automation
includes.description: Automate multiple pipeline activities through generalized search and limited-code model development.

includes.label: In-house preparation and modeling scripts
includes.description: Recurring data-science preparation and modeling work is automated through internally written scripts.

includes.label: Automated feature selection
includes.description: Feature selection is performed automatically within the modeling workflow.

includes.label: Automated model training
includes.description: Model training is run automatically as a recurring modeling activity.

clusters.name: Feature Storage Technology and Abstraction
clusters.description: Which storage technologies or data-engineering abstractions implement feature storage?

values.label: Shared feature-store abstraction
values.description: A centralized feature-store interface defines features and generates training data, without an explicitly combined multi-technology storage layer.

includes.label: Feature-store data-engineering abstraction
includes.description: Centralize feature definition and training-data generation behind a shared feature-store interface.

clusters.name: Pipeline Task Orchestration
clusters.description: Which mechanism coordinates dependent ML tasks and workflow steps?

relations.reading: Pipeline Task Orchestration requires Compute Runtime Location to be decided first
relations.rationale: Scheduling and event coordination must target an available execution environment and its resource model.

relations.reading: Choices on Pipeline Task Orchestration affect the outcomes of Data Ingestion and Transformation Strategy
relations.rationale: Trigger and dependency choices determine when preparation, synchronization, and replication occur.

values.label: Dependency-orchestrated workflow
values.description: An orchestration mechanism coordinates dependent ML tasks through explicit workflow dependencies and schedules them on compute infrastructure.

includes.label: Task dependency orchestration
includes.description: Feature engineering, training, and prediction are scheduled through explicit dependencies on compute infrastructure.

values.label: Script-led workflow with orchestration support
values.description: Practitioners coordinate ML steps primarily through manually executed scripts, optionally combining them with explicit task dependencies or infrastructure orchestration.

includes.label: Task dependency orchestration
includes.description: Feature engineering, training, and prediction are scheduled through explicit dependencies on compute infrastructure.

includes.label: Manual script-driven ML workflow
includes.description: Coordinate data preparation, training, and validation through manually executed scripts and transitions.

clusters.name: Training and Release Cadence
clusters.description: Which cadence governs model training and production release?

values.label: Continuous training with infrequent production release
values.description: Models are updated through a continuous or recurring training pipeline, but production releases occur only occasionally and may follow a manually coordinated lifecycle.

includes.label: Infrequent model release cadence
includes.description: Coordinate a lifecycle in which models are retrained and deployed only occasionally.

includes.label: Continuous training pipeline
includes.description: A pipeline that repeatedly updates models as new examples or fresh data arrive.

clusters.name: Execution Triggering
clusters.description: What event or schedule initiates ML pipeline execution?

relations.reading: Choices on Execution Triggering affect the outcomes of Compute Runtime Location
relations.rationale: Scheduled, batch, and stream triggers influence the runtime context used for execution.

values.label: Batch-triggered execution
values.description: Processing functions are initiated as scheduled or dataset-oriented batch jobs.

values.label: Kafka-stream triggering
values.description: Processing functions are initiated by events arriving on Kafka or comparable streams.

values.label: Schedule-or-trigger production execution
values.description: Production training or execution starts on a schedule or in response to a trigger.

values.label: Model-decay retraining triggering
values.description: Initiate retraining when a model-decay measure indicates degraded performance.

values.label: New-data retraining triggering
values.description: Initiate retraining when newly available data satisfies the retraining condition.

clusters.name: Compute Runtime Location
clusters.description: Where do ML processing and training execute across local, edge, distributed, and endpoint environments?

relations.reading: Choices on Compute Runtime Location limit the options available on Pipeline Task Orchestration
relations.rationale: Runtime capabilities and resource models limit which scheduling, event, and scaling mechanisms are practical.

relations.reading: Choices on Compute Runtime Location affect the outcomes of Model Packaging Format
relations.rationale: Infrastructure choices determine available deployment resources, latency, scalability, and operational maintenance requirements.

values.label: Local notebook runtime
values.description: Processing is initially validated in a local notebook environment.

clusters.name: Compute Runtime Management
clusters.description: How are distributed compute runtimes provisioned and operated?

values.label: Multi-mode Spark and engine runtime
values.description: Distributed computation is provisioned and operated through a combination of serverless Spark execution, operator-managed Spark clusters, and interchangeable computation engines.

includes.label: Distributed serverless Spark runtime
includes.description: Spark-backed processing runs on a distributed cluster through a serverless-style client without redesigning the task.

includes.label: Operator-managed Spark cluster
includes.description: A Kubernetes operator launches and manages the Spark cluster used for processing.

includes.label: Pluggable heterogeneous computation engines
includes.description: The runtime platform supports multiple interchangeable engines for distributed and real-time workloads.

clusters.name: ML Coding Environment
clusters.description: Which language, development medium, and coding environment are used to build ML software?

relations.reading: Choices on ML Coding Environment affect the outcomes of ML Platform Composition
relations.rationale: Engineering practices influence reproducibility, buildability, deployment automation, and the feasibility of productionizing artifacts.

values.label: IDE-and-notebook workflow profile
values.description: Python ML software is developed through an IDE and Jupyter notebooks, including notebook-oriented production workflows and direct cell-based query execution.

includes.label: IDE-based Python development
includes.description: Use an IDE such as PyCharm to develop reproducible Python ML software.

includes.label: Jupyter exploratory environment
includes.description: Jupyter notebooks support exploratory analysis, research, data stories, and result sharing.

includes.label: Notebook-based production pipelines
includes.description: Using Jupyter notebooks as the implementation medium for serious production pipelines is explicitly declined.

includes.label: Notebook cell-magic query execution
includes.description: Embed specialized query execution directly in notebook cells rather than reusable production functions.

values.label: Scripted-production notebook-tooling profile
values.description: Exploration remains notebook-based, while production execution uses Python scripts and notebook work is supported by linting, alternative notebook tooling, and—where applicable—cell-based query execution.

includes.label: Jupyter exploratory environment
includes.description: Jupyter notebooks support exploratory analysis, research, data stories, and result sharing.

includes.label: Python-script production pipelines
includes.description: Frequently executed production pipelines are implemented as Python scripts rather than notebooks.

includes.label: Notebook-based production pipelines
includes.description: Using Jupyter notebooks as the implementation medium for serious production pipelines is explicitly declined.

includes.label: IDE-integrated linting
includes.description: Code editors provide linting and style correction that notebook environments commonly lack.

includes.label: Alternative notebook workflow tooling
includes.description: Use tools such as pynb or Hydrogen to extend or replace conventional notebook workflows.

includes.label: Notebook cell-magic query execution
includes.description: Embed specialized query execution directly in notebook cells rather than reusable production functions.

clusters.name: ML Testing and Validation
clusters.description: Which testing and validation practices establish ML software and deployment readiness?

values.label: Test-driven pipeline development
values.description: Production data pipelines are developed with tests, fixtures, and software-engineering practices.

values.label: Automated CI and testing validation
values.description: Validate ML changes through continuous integration and automated testing suites.

values.label: Predictive-performance deployment gate
values.description: Require model performance evidence before promoting a model into production service.

values.label: Continuous testing as sole lifecycle practice
values.description: Rely on continuous testing without continuous training and validation for ML lifecycle assurance.

values.label: Development-production reproducibility parity
values.description: Development and production dependencies, procedures, and model inputs are kept equivalent to reproduce results reliably.

values.label: High-coverage preparation testing
values.description: Data preparation pipelines are developed with extensive automated testing and code coverage.

clusters.name: ML Development and Release Process
clusters.description: Which development and delivery process structures ML work from experimentation through production?

values.label: Iterative bidirectional process model
values.description: Data-science work follows an iterative process in which phases can be revisited and refined.

values.label: Process-architecture separation
values.description: Treating process modeling as separate from technology and non-functional architectural decisions is rejected.

values.label: Flexible data-science process
values.description: The process model accommodates rapidly changing data-science technologies and requirements.

values.label: Semi-automated environment promotion
values.description: Deploy automatically to test environments while promoting manually or semi-manually across higher environments.

values.label: Experimentation workflow orchestration
values.description: Iterative algorithm and modeling experiments are coordinated before producing pipeline code.

clusters.name: Model Packaging Format
clusters.description: Which artifact format bundles or serializes trained models for deployment and interchange?

values.label: File-based model packaging
values.description: A model is packaged as a file and loaded by a model server.

values.label: Containerized model packaging
values.description: Models are packaged as container images for deployment to serving infrastructure.

clusters.name: Model Serving Strategy
clusters.description: How are packaged models hosted, exposed, and restored as prediction services?

relations.reading: Model Serving Strategy requires ML Platform Composition to be decided first
relations.rationale: The feedback split separates hosting strategy from the delivery architecture that assembles and operates it.

relations.reading: Choices on Model Serving Strategy affect the outcomes of Production Model Monitoring
relations.rationale: Serving topology and deployment pattern determine observable operational behavior.

values.label: Platform-managed API serving
values.description: A managed ML platform automatically exposes trained models through an API.

values.label: Model-as-a-Service deployment
values.description: A dedicated prediction service exposes a model independently from consuming applications.

values.label: Shadow, competing-model, and traffic-split deployment
values.description: Validate or operate model versions through shadowing, A/B traffic splitting, or simultaneous competing-model service.

values.label: Client-server model-serving architecture
values.description: Deploy predictions through a client-request and continuously available server-response architecture.

values.label: Retraining-or-rollback restoration strategy
values.description: Restore service by either retraining and redeploying or rolling back to the previous model version.

values.label: Progressive canary rollout and rollback
values.description: Expose candidate models to selected users progressively, compare impact, promote after confirmation, and roll back on failure.

values.label: Direct offline-model deployment
values.description: Deploy an offline-trained model directly as a prediction service without additional retraining, validation, or delivery automation.

clusters.name: Prediction Interface
clusters.description: Which interface and interaction pattern do consumers use to call model predictions?

values.label: REST service endpoint
values.description: Consumers call a model through a REST-based prediction service that returns results on request.

includes.label: REST prediction API
includes.description: A REST interface provides predictions and retrieves model parameters or contextual features.

clusters.name: Prediction Access Control and Contract
clusters.description: How are prediction consumers authenticated and constrained by service access contracts?

values.label: Prediction-service contract and load access
values.description: Prediction APIs are accessed through contract checks, authentication, and operational load validation.

clusters.name: ML Platform Composition
clusters.description: Which platform arrangement assembles ML capabilities into an integrated or custom-built operational ecosystem?

relations.reading: Choices on ML Platform Composition affect the outcomes of Production Model Monitoring
relations.rationale: Platform topology determines monitoring integration, operational burden, deployment repeatability, and governance exposure.

relations.reading: Choices on ML Platform Composition limit the options available on ML Asset Collaboration
relations.rationale: Platform choices constrain how repositories, environments, artifacts, and shared development workflows are integrated.

values.label: End-to-end MLOps platform
values.description: A unified platform automates the ML lifecycle from development through deployment and operations without requiring a broader architectural emphasis.

includes.label: End-to-end MLOps platform
includes.description: A unified platform automates technical work across model development, deployment, and operations.

values.label: Integrated or composable MLOps ecosystem
values.description: An ecosystem combines platform or provider-suite capabilities with selected separately assembled tools, allowing the arrangement to be tailored to organizational needs.

includes.label: End-to-end MLOps platform
includes.description: A unified platform automates technical work across model development, deployment, and operations.

includes.label: Integrated MLOps suite
includes.description: A single provider suite covers model building, training, deployment, and monitoring.

includes.label: Custom-built MLOps tool ecosystem
includes.description: Assemble separate tools rather than adopting one end-to-end managed MLOps platform.

values.label: Production-first MLOps architecture
values.description: A production-oriented arrangement designs operational requirements into the ML architecture from the outset, potentially combining platform, suite, and custom tooling capabilities.

includes.label: End-to-end MLOps platform
includes.description: A unified platform automates technical work across model development, deployment, and operations.

includes.label: Integrated MLOps suite
includes.description: A single provider suite covers model building, training, deployment, and monitoring.

includes.label: Production-oriented architecture
includes.description: Production requirements are incorporated into architecture from the beginning.

clusters.name: ML Service Decomposition
clusters.description: How are ML capabilities divided into services, modules, or shared architectural units?

values.label: Managed-service pipeline composition
values.description: ML capabilities are divided across separate managed services for processing, building, deployment, and operational monitoring, without prescribing finer-grained application modularity.

includes.label: Cloud-native service composition
includes.description: Separate managed services provide data processing, building, testing, deployment, and monitoring capabilities.

values.label: Hybrid business-service ML architecture
values.description: ML capabilities are composed as network-accessible services with separate training and serving, combining shared-codebase functionality with independently operating services organized around business concerns.

includes.label: Cloud-native service composition
includes.description: Separate managed services provide data processing, building, testing, deployment, and monitoring capabilities.

includes.label: Software architecture granularity
includes.description: Architectural selection varies application modularity and granularity.

includes.label: Network-based service composition
includes.description: Compose independent ML application components through network communication and service-layer agreements.

includes.label: Separated training and serving architecture
includes.description: Keep model training and prediction serving as distinct production stages.

includes.label: Monolithic shared-codebase architecture
includes.description: Keep business concerns and functionality in one codebase to reuse boilerplate and simplify development.

includes.label: Business-concern microservice decomposition
includes.description: Separate functionality into independently operating services organized around business concerns.

clusters.name: ML Deployment Orchestration
clusters.description: How are ML artifacts and deployments coordinated across infrastructure and delivery workflows?

values.label: Platform-orchestrated continuous delivery
values.description: ML deployments are coordinated through a container-orchestration platform, with continuous delivery workflows integrated into the platform. This option covers Kubernetes-based execution and delivery coordination across infrastructure.

includes.label: Kubernetes-based deployment orchestration
includes.description: Kubeflow Pipelines orchestrate ML deployments on Google Kubernetes Engine.

includes.label: Continuous delivery orchestration
includes.description: Continuous delivery workflows coordinate repetitive build, validation, packaging, and release activities.

values.label: Artifact-promoted continuous delivery
values.description: ML deployments are coordinated as continuous delivery workflows that build, validate, package, and promote deployable artifacts into target environments. The emphasis is on delivery-pipeline coordination rather than a specific infrastructure orchestrator.

includes.label: Artifact-based continuous delivery
includes.description: Build-produced packages, executables, images, and other artifacts are promoted into target environments.

includes.label: Continuous delivery orchestration
includes.description: Continuous delivery workflows coordinate repetitive build, validation, packaging, and release activities.

clusters.name: Infrastructure Placement
clusters.description: Where are ML platforms and sensitive data hosted across cloud, on-premises, and hybrid locations?

values.label: Hybrid cloud and on-premises infrastructure
values.description: ML operations span cloud and retained on-premises infrastructure.

clusters.name: Infrastructure Operating Model
clusters.description: Who builds, manages, and operates the ML infrastructure and platform?

values.label: Fully managed platform
values.description: Organizations adopt a fully managed platform for infrastructure and ML operations.

values.label: Separated ML and application responsibilities
values.description: Assign model complexity to data scientists and user-experience complexity to application developers.

clusters.name: Production Model Monitoring
clusters.description: Which operational signals and diagnostic mechanisms assess deployed model behavior over time?

relations.reading: Choices on Production Model Monitoring affect the outcomes of Model Adoption and Value Realization
relations.rationale: Monitoring, transparency, fairness, and stakeholder involvement affect trust, adoption, and realized production value.

relations.reading: Choices on Production Model Monitoring limit the options available on Model Packaging Format
relations.rationale: Security, observability, and governance requirements restrict acceptable serving interfaces and deployment behaviors.

values.label: Basic production performance monitoring
values.description: Operational signals track deployed-model performance, live behavior, drift, and data-quality issues over time, without necessarily adding broader diagnostic mechanisms.

includes.label: Production performance, drift, and data-quality monitoring
includes.description: Operational monitoring tracks deployed-model performance, live traffic, drift, anomalies, and data-quality violations.

values.label: Health-augmented production monitoring
values.description: Production performance and data-quality monitoring is augmented with model and service health checks, operational diagnostics, and related runtime signals.

includes.label: Production performance, drift, and data-quality monitoring
includes.description: Operational monitoring tracks deployed-model performance, live traffic, drift, anomalies, and data-quality violations.

includes.label: Health and diagnostic operations
includes.description: Production operations include model health checks and diagnostic capabilities.

values.label: Consistency- and dependency-aware monitoring
values.description: Monitoring additionally validates training-serving consistency and observes external data dependencies that can affect deployed behavior.

includes.label: Production performance, drift, and data-quality monitoring
includes.description: Operational monitoring tracks deployed-model performance, live traffic, drift, anomalies, and data-quality violations.

includes.label: Health and diagnostic operations
includes.description: Production operations include model health checks and diagnostic capabilities.

includes.label: Training-serving consistency validation
includes.description: Validation that training and serving produce consistent inputs, features, and predictions.

includes.label: Data dependency monitoring
includes.description: External data sources and pipelines are monitored as operational dependencies of deployed ML systems.

values.label: Comprehensive production observability
values.description: An integrated monitoring arrangement combines performance, health, consistency, dependency, and persisted prediction evidence for ongoing assessment and comparison.

includes.label: Production performance, drift, and data-quality monitoring
includes.description: Operational monitoring tracks deployed-model performance, live traffic, drift, anomalies, and data-quality violations.

includes.label: Health and diagnostic operations
includes.description: Production operations include model health checks and diagnostic capabilities.

includes.label: Training-serving consistency validation
includes.description: Validation that training and serving produce consistent inputs, features, and predictions.

includes.label: Data dependency monitoring
includes.description: External data sources and pipelines are monitored as operational dependencies of deployed ML systems.

includes.label: Prediction and candidate-output persistence
includes.description: Persist production inputs, live predictions, and shadow candidate predictions for later monitoring and comparison.

clusters.name: Model Governance and Accountability
clusters.description: How are regulatory alignment, monitoring ownership, and long-term accountability established?

values.label: Regulatory and business alignment
values.description: MLOps practices align deployed models with organizational needs and regulatory requirements.

clusters.name: Model Adoption and Value Realization
clusters.description: Documents vary in how organizations move models from experiments into sustained use through transparency, stakeholder engagement, collaboration, and demonstrated value.

values.label: Operational value realization
values.description: Models are moved into operational use to solve business problems and generate measurable value. The emphasis is on deployment and sustained use rather than on broader adoption practices.

includes.label: Production use for value realization
includes.description: Models create meaningful value only when deployed and actually used in operational settings.

clusters.name: ML Asset Versioning
clusters.description: Which ML code, data, and model artifacts are versioned and retained for reproducibility?

values.label: Comprehensive ML artifact versioning
values.description: Source code, datasets, models, schemas, executables, and dependencies are versioned and retained through version-control and artifact-management systems to support reproducibility.

includes.label: Versioned ML artifacts
includes.description: Source code, data, models, schemas, executables, and dependencies are managed through version control and artifact repositories.

includes.label: Source-controlled ML pipeline code
includes.description: Pipeline and application source code is stored in version-controlled repositories for collaboration and delivery.

clusters.name: ML Architecture Governance
clusters.description: How are ML solution architecture and process standards defined, reviewed, and traced?

values.label: Predefined architecture and process framework
values.description: A predefined framework guides architectural decisions and systematic treatment of non-functional requirements.

clusters.name: Model Family and Objective Selection
clusters.description: Which model family, ensemble approach, or prioritized objective guides model selection?

relations.reading: Choices on Model Family and Objective Selection affect the outcomes of Model Packaging Format
relations.rationale: Model complexity and optimization choices influence deployability and serving requirements.

values.label: Automated model-family selection
values.description: AutoML selects among alternative model families as part of pipeline construction.

values.label: Model ensembling
values.description: Multiple models are combined to improve predictive stability or score.

values.label: Explicit model-objective prioritization
values.description: Teams choose which quality objective, such as false-negative minimization, to optimize.

clusters.name: Hyperparameter and Architecture Optimization
clusters.description: How are hyperparameters and model architectures searched, tuned, and evaluated for practical deployment?

values.label: Manual hyperparameter tuning
values.description: Practitioners tune model hyperparameters by hand and trial and error for smaller modeling tasks.

values.label: Automated hyperparameter optimization
values.description: Search procedures automatically optimize model hyperparameters when manual exploration is impractical.

clusters.name: ML Execution Caching and Resumption
clusters.description: Which mechanisms cache, retain, and resume intermediate ML execution state?

values.label: Application-managed persistent caching
values.description: Applications explicitly persist reusable computation results in files, buckets, or databases.

values.label: ElastiCache model state
values.description: Current model parameters and inference features are retrieved from an in-memory store.

clusters.name: ML Metadata, Metrics, and Artifact Tracking
clusters.description: Which mechanisms record ML metadata, metrics, and versioned artifacts for reproducibility and operations?

values.label: Comprehensive pipeline lifecycle tracking
values.description: A metadata-backed system captures pipeline executions, metrics, experiments, lineage, parameters, and versioned artifacts across the ML lifecycle.

includes.label: ML metadata store
includes.description: A metadata store records pipeline executions, parameters, metrics, lineage, and comparison context.

includes.label: Training and testing metric recording
includes.description: Training and test metrics are retained to compare newly trained and previous models.

includes.label: Pipeline execution metadata capture
includes.description: Capture execution timing, parameters, and run metadata for pipeline and experiment tracking.

includes.label: Version-controlled data and model artifacts
includes.description: Data inputs, generated models, and pipeline artifacts are versioned for reproducibility.

includes.label: Experiment and training-run tracking
includes.description: Experiments and training runs are recorded and organized to compare models and support reproducibility.

clusters.name: Online Model Update Strategy
clusters.description: Which learning and parameter-update approach adapts models to incoming data while supporting prediction serving?

relations.reading: Choices on Online Model Update Strategy affect the outcomes of Production Model Monitoring
relations.rationale: Incremental updates, persistence, and atomicity determine what drift, staleness, and consistency signals monitoring must observe.

values.label: Incremental linear learning
values.description: Linear or logistic learners update rapidly from incoming examples for online learning.

values.label: Periodic model-parameter persistence
values.description: Learned parameters are periodically persisted so real-time prediction workers can use current model state.

clusters.name: Data Processing Mode
clusters.description: Which temporal execution mode processes data for training, feature generation, or prediction?

relations.reading: Choices on Data Processing Mode limit the options available on Feature Computation Timing
relations.rationale: Batch, real-time, near-real-time, and streaming modes constrain whether features are precomputed, asynchronous, or request-time.

values.label: Batch processing
values.description: Process data as discrete jobs or recurring offline runs.

values.label: Real-time processing
values.description: Process data continuously with minimal delay while it moves through the pipeline.

values.label: Offline versus real-time execution placement
values.description: Risk workloads execute offline or in real time according to urgency and computational requirements.

includes.description: Centralize feature definition and training-data generation behind a shared feature-store interface.

selected_clusters.name: Pipeline Task Orchestration
selected_clusters.description: Which mechanism coordinates dependent ML tasks and workflow steps?

relations.reading: Pipeline Task Orchestration requires Compute Runtime Location to be decided first
relations.rationale: Scheduling and event coordination must target an available execution environment and its resource model.

relations.reading: Choices on Pipeline Task Orchestration affect the outcomes of Data Ingestion and Transformation Strategy
relations.rationale: Trigger and dependency choices determine when preparation, synchronization, and replication occur.

values.label: Dependency-orchestrated workflow
values.description: An orchestration mechanism coordinates dependent ML tasks through explicit workflow dependencies and schedules them on compute infrastructure.

includes.label: Task dependency orchestration
includes.description: Feature engineering, training, and prediction are scheduled through explicit dependencies on compute infrastructure.

values.label: Script-led workflow with orchestration support
values.description: Practitioners coordinate ML steps primarily through manually executed scripts, optionally combining them with explicit task dependencies or infrastructure orchestration.

includes.label: Task dependency orchestration
includes.description: Feature engineering, training, and prediction are scheduled through explicit dependencies on compute infrastructure.

includes.label: Manual script-driven ML workflow
includes.description: Coordinate data preparation, training, and validation through manually executed scripts and transitions.

selected_clusters.name: Training and Release Cadence
selected_clusters.description: Which cadence governs model training and production release?

values.label: Continuous training with infrequent production release
values.description: Models are updated through a continuous or recurring training pipeline, but production releases occur only occasionally and may follow a manually coordinated lifecycle.

includes.label: Infrequent model release cadence
includes.description: Coordinate a lifecycle in which models are retrained and deployed only occasionally.

includes.label: Continuous training pipeline
includes.description: A pipeline that repeatedly updates models as new examples or fresh data arrive.

selected_clusters.name: Execution Triggering
selected_clusters.description: What event or schedule initiates ML pipeline execution?

relations.reading: Choices on Execution Triggering affect the outcomes of Compute Runtime Location
relations.rationale: Scheduled, batch, and stream triggers influence the runtime context used for execution.

values.label: Batch-triggered execution
values.description: Processing functions are initiated as scheduled or dataset-oriented batch jobs.

values.label: Kafka-stream triggering
values.description: Processing functions are initiated by events arriving on Kafka or comparable streams.

values.label: Schedule-or-trigger production execution
values.description: Production training or execution starts on a schedule or in response to a trigger.

values.label: Model-decay retraining triggering
values.description: Initiate retraining when a model-decay measure indicates degraded performance.

values.label: New-data retraining triggering
values.description: Initiate retraining when newly available data satisfies the retraining condition.

selected_clusters.name: Compute Runtime Location
selected_clusters.description: Where do ML processing and training execute across local, edge, distributed, and endpoint environments?

relations.reading: Choices on Compute Runtime Location limit the options available on Pipeline Task Orchestration
relations.rationale: Runtime capabilities and resource models limit which scheduling, event, and scaling mechanisms are practical.

relations.reading: Choices on Compute Runtime Location affect the outcomes of Model Packaging Format
relations.rationale: Infrastructure choices determine available deployment resources, latency, scalability, and operational maintenance requirements.

values.label: Local notebook runtime
values.description: Processing is initially validated in a local notebook environment.

selected_clusters.name: Compute Runtime Management
selected_clusters.description: How are distributed compute runtimes provisioned and operated?

values.label: Multi-mode Spark and engine runtime
values.description: Distributed computation is provisioned and operated through a combination of serverless Spark execution, operator-managed Spark clusters, and interchangeable computation engines.

includes.label: Distributed serverless Spark runtime
includes.description: Spark-backed processing runs on a distributed cluster through a serverless-style client without redesigning the task.

includes.label: Operator-managed Spark cluster
includes.description: A Kubernetes operator launches and manages the Spark cluster used for processing.

includes.label: Pluggable heterogeneous computation engines
includes.description: The runtime platform supports multiple interchangeable engines for distributed and real-time workloads.

selected_clusters.name: ML Coding Environment
selected_clusters.description: Which language, development medium, and coding environment are used to build ML software?

relations.reading: Choices on ML Coding Environment affect the outcomes of ML Platform Composition
relations.rationale: Engineering practices influence reproducibility, buildability, deployment automation, and the feasibility of productionizing artifacts.

values.label: IDE-and-notebook workflow profile
values.description: Python ML software is developed through an IDE and Jupyter notebooks, including notebook-oriented production workflows and direct cell-based query execution.

includes.label: IDE-based Python development
includes.description: Use an IDE such as PyCharm to develop reproducible Python ML software.

includes.label: Jupyter exploratory environment
includes.description: Jupyter notebooks support exploratory analysis, research, data stories, and result sharing.

includes.label: Notebook-based production pipelines
includes.description: Using Jupyter notebooks as the implementation medium for serious production pipelines is explicitly declined.

includes.label: Notebook cell-magic query execution
includes.description: Embed specialized query execution directly in notebook cells rather than reusable production functions.

values.label: Scripted-production notebook-tooling profile
values.description: Exploration remains notebook-based, while production execution uses Python scripts and notebook work is supported by linting, alternative notebook tooling, and—where applicable—cell-based query execution.

includes.label: Jupyter exploratory environment
includes.description: Jupyter notebooks support exploratory analysis, research, data stories, and result sharing.

includes.label: Python-script production pipelines
includes.description: Frequently executed production pipelines are implemented as Python scripts rather than notebooks.

includes.label: Notebook-based production pipelines
includes.description: Using Jupyter notebooks as the implementation medium for serious production pipelines is explicitly declined.

includes.label: IDE-integrated linting
includes.description: Code editors provide linting and style correction that notebook environments commonly lack.

includes.label: Alternative notebook workflow tooling
includes.description: Use tools such as pynb or Hydrogen to extend or replace conventional notebook workflows.

includes.label: Notebook cell-magic query execution
includes.description: Embed specialized query execution directly in notebook cells rather than reusable production functions.

selected_clusters.name: ML Testing and Validation
selected_clusters.description: Which testing and validation practices establish ML software and deployment readiness?

values.label: Test-driven pipeline development
values.description: Production data pipelines are developed with tests, fixtures, and software-engineering practices.

values.label: Automated CI and testing validation
values.description: Validate ML changes through continuous integration and automated testing suites.

values.label: Predictive-performance deployment gate
values.description: Require model performance evidence before promoting a model into production service.

values.label: Continuous testing as sole lifecycle practice
values.description: Rely on continuous testing without continuous training and validation for ML lifecycle assurance.

values.label: Development-production reproducibility parity
values.description: Development and production dependencies, procedures, and model inputs are kept equivalent to reproduce results reliably.

values.label: High-coverage preparation testing
values.description: Data preparation pipelines are developed with extensive automated testing and code coverage.

selected_clusters.name: ML Development and Release Process
selected_clusters.description: Which development and delivery process structures ML work from experimentation through production?

values.label: Iterative bidirectional process model
values.description: Data-science work follows an iterative process in which phases can be revisited and refined.

values.label: Process-architecture separation
values.description: Treating process modeling as separate from technology and non-functional architectural decisions is rejected.

values.label: Flexible data-science process
values.description: The process model accommodates rapidly changing data-science technologies and requirements.

values.label: Semi-automated environment promotion
values.description: Deploy automatically to test environments while promoting manually or semi-manually across higher environments.

values.label: Experimentation workflow orchestration
values.description: Iterative algorithm and modeling experiments are coordinated before producing pipeline code.

selected_clusters.name: Model Packaging Format
selected_clusters.description: Which artifact format bundles or serializes trained models for deployment and interchange?

values.label: File-based model packaging
values.description: A model is packaged as a file and loaded by a model server.

values.label: Containerized model packaging
values.description: Models are packaged as container images for deployment to serving infrastructure.

selected_clusters.name: Model Serving Strategy
selected_clusters.description: How are packaged models hosted, exposed, and restored as prediction services?

relations.reading: Model Serving Strategy requires ML Platform Composition to be decided first
relations.rationale: The feedback split separates hosting strategy from the delivery architecture that assembles and operates it.

relations.reading: Choices on Model Serving Strategy affect the outcomes of Production Model Monitoring
relations.rationale: Serving topology and deployment pattern determine observable operational behavior.

values.label: Platform-managed API serving
values.description: A managed ML platform automatically exposes trained models through an API.

values.label: Model-as-a-Service deployment
values.description: A dedicated prediction service exposes a model independently from consuming applications.

values.label: Shadow, competing-model, and traffic-split deployment
values.description: Validate or operate model versions through shadowing, A/B traffic splitting, or simultaneous competing-model service.

values.label: Client-server model-serving architecture
values.description: Deploy predictions through a client-request and continuously available server-response architecture.

values.label: Retraining-or-rollback restoration strategy
values.description: Restore service by either retraining and redeploying or rolling back to the previous model version.

values.label: Progressive canary rollout and rollback
values.description: Expose candidate models to selected users progressively, compare impact, promote after confirmation, and roll back on failure.

values.label: Direct offline-model deployment
values.description: Deploy an offline-trained model directly as a prediction service without additional retraining, validation, or delivery automation.

selected_clusters.name: Prediction Interface
selected_clusters.description: Which interface and interaction pattern do consumers use to call model predictions?

values.label: REST service endpoint
values.description: Consumers call a model through a REST-based prediction service that returns results on request.

includes.label: REST prediction API
includes.description: A REST interface provides predictions and retrieves model parameters or contextual features.

selected_clusters.name: Prediction Access Control and Contract
selected_clusters.description: How are prediction consumers authenticated and constrained by service access contracts?

values.label: Prediction-service contract and load access
values.description: Prediction APIs are accessed through contract checks, authentication, and operational load validation.

selected_clusters.name: ML Platform Composition
selected_clusters.description: Which platform arrangement assembles ML capabilities into an integrated or custom-built operational ecosystem?

relations.reading: Choices on ML Platform Composition affect the outcomes of Production Model Monitoring
relations.rationale: Platform topology determines monitoring integration, operational burden, deployment repeatability, and governance exposure.

relations.reading: Choices on ML Platform Composition limit the options available on ML Asset Collaboration
relations.rationale: Platform choices constrain how repositories, environments, artifacts, and shared development workflows are integrated.

values.label: End-to-end MLOps platform
values.description: A unified platform automates the ML lifecycle from development through deployment and operations without requiring a broader architectural emphasis.

includes.label: End-to-end MLOps platform
includes.description: A unified platform automates technical work across model development, deployment, and operations.

values.label: Integrated or composable MLOps ecosystem
values.description: An ecosystem combines platform or provider-suite capabilities with selected separately assembled tools, allowing the arrangement to be tailored to organizational needs.

includes.label: End-to-end MLOps platform
includes.description: A unified platform automates technical work across model development, deployment, and operations.

includes.label: Integrated MLOps suite
includes.description: A single provider suite covers model building, training, deployment, and monitoring.

includes.label: Custom-built MLOps tool ecosystem
includes.description: Assemble separate tools rather than adopting one end-to-end managed MLOps platform.

values.label: Production-first MLOps architecture
values.description: A production-oriented arrangement designs operational requirements into the ML architecture from the outset, potentially combining platform, suite, and custom tooling capabilities.

includes.label: End-to-end MLOps platform
includes.description: A unified platform automates technical work across model development, deployment, and operations.

includes.label: Integrated MLOps suite
includes.description: A single provider suite covers model building, training, deployment, and monitoring.

includes.label: Production-oriented architecture
includes.description: Production requirements are incorporated into architecture from the beginning.

selected_clusters.name: ML Service Decomposition
selected_clusters.description: How are ML capabilities divided into services, modules, or shared architectural units?

values.label: Managed-service pipeline composition
values.description: ML capabilities are divided across separate managed services for processing, building, deployment, and operational monitoring, without prescribing finer-grained application modularity.

includes.label: Cloud-native service composition
includes.description: Separate managed services provide data processing, building, testing, deployment, and monitoring capabilities.

values.label: Hybrid business-service ML architecture
values.description: ML capabilities are composed as network-accessible services with separate training and serving, combining shared-codebase functionality with independently operating services organized around business concerns.

includes.label: Cloud-native service composition
includes.description: Separate managed services provide data processing, building, testing, deployment, and monitoring capabilities.

includes.label: Software architecture granularity
includes.description: Architectural selection varies application modularity and granularity.

includes.label: Network-based service composition
includes.description: Compose independent ML application components through network communication and service-layer agreements.

includes.label: Separated training and serving architecture
includes.description: Keep model training and prediction serving as distinct production stages.

includes.label: Monolithic shared-codebase architecture
includes.description: Keep business concerns and functionality in one codebase to reuse boilerplate and simplify development.

includes.label: Business-concern microservice decomposition
includes.description: Separate functionality into independently operating services organized around business concerns.

selected_clusters.name: ML Deployment Orchestration
selected_clusters.description: How are ML artifacts and deployments coordinated across infrastructure and delivery workflows?

values.label: Platform-orchestrated continuous delivery
values.description: ML deployments are coordinated through a container-orchestration platform, with continuous delivery workflows integrated into the platform. This option covers Kubernetes-based execution and delivery coordination across infrastructure.

includes.label: Kubernetes-based deployment orchestration
includes.description: Kubeflow Pipelines orchestrate ML deployments on Google Kubernetes Engine.

includes.label: Continuous delivery orchestration
includes.description: Continuous delivery workflows coordinate repetitive build, validation, packaging, and release activities.

values.label: Artifact-promoted continuous delivery
values.description: ML deployments are coordinated as continuous delivery workflows that build, validate, package, and promote deployable artifacts into target environments. The emphasis is on delivery-pipeline coordination rather than a specific infrastructure orchestrator.

includes.label: Artifact-based continuous delivery
includes.description: Build-produced packages, executables, images, and other artifacts are promoted into target environments.

includes.label: Continuous delivery orchestration
includes.description: Continuous delivery workflows coordinate repetitive build, validation, packaging, and release activities.

selected_clusters.name: Infrastructure Placement
selected_clusters.description: Where are ML platforms and sensitive data hosted across cloud, on-premises, and hybrid locations?

values.label: Hybrid cloud and on-premises infrastructure
values.description: ML operations span cloud and retained on-premises infrastructure.

selected_clusters.name: Infrastructure Operating Model
selected_clusters.description: Who builds, manages, and operates the ML infrastructure and platform?

values.label: Fully managed platform
values.description: Organizations adopt a fully managed platform for infrastructure and ML operations.

values.label: Separated ML and application responsibilities
values.description: Assign model complexity to data scientists and user-experience complexity to application developers.

selected_clusters.name: Production Model Monitoring
selected_clusters.description: Which operational signals and diagnostic mechanisms assess deployed model behavior over time?

relations.reading: Choices on Production Model Monitoring affect the outcomes of Model Adoption and Value Realization
relations.rationale: Monitoring, transparency, fairness, and stakeholder involvement affect trust, adoption, and realized production value.

relations.reading: Choices on Production Model Monitoring limit the options available on Model Packaging Format
relations.rationale: Security, observability, and governance requirements restrict acceptable serving interfaces and deployment behaviors.

values.label: Basic production performance monitoring
values.description: Operational signals track deployed-model performance, live behavior, drift, and data-quality issues over time, without necessarily adding broader diagnostic mechanisms.

includes.label: Production performance, drift, and data-quality monitoring
includes.description: Operational monitoring tracks deployed-model performance, live traffic, drift, anomalies, and data-quality violations.

values.label: Health-augmented production monitoring
values.description: Production performance and data-quality monitoring is augmented with model and service health checks, operational diagnostics, and related runtime signals.

includes.label: Production performance, drift, and data-quality monitoring
includes.description: Operational monitoring tracks deployed-model performance, live traffic, drift, anomalies, and data-quality violations.

includes.label: Health and diagnostic operations
includes.description: Production operations include model health checks and diagnostic capabilities.

values.label: Consistency- and dependency-aware monitoring
values.description: Monitoring additionally validates training-serving consistency and observes external data dependencies that can affect deployed behavior.

includes.label: Production performance, drift, and data-quality monitoring
includes.description: Operational monitoring tracks deployed-model performance, live traffic, drift, anomalies, and data-quality violations.

includes.label: Health and diagnostic operations
includes.description: Production operations include model health checks and diagnostic capabilities.

includes.label: Training-serving consistency validation
includes.description: Validation that training and serving produce consistent inputs, features, and predictions.

includes.label: Data dependency monitoring
includes.description: External data sources and pipelines are monitored as operational dependencies of deployed ML systems.

values.label: Comprehensive production observability
values.description: An integrated monitoring arrangement combines performance, health, consistency, dependency, and persisted prediction evidence for ongoing assessment and comparison.

includes.label: Production performance, drift, and data-quality monitoring
includes.description: Operational monitoring tracks deployed-model performance, live traffic, drift, anomalies, and data-quality violations.

includes.label: Health and diagnostic operations
includes.description: Production operations include model health checks and diagnostic capabilities.

includes.label: Training-serving consistency validation
includes.description: Validation that training and serving produce consistent inputs, features, and predictions.

includes.label: Data dependency monitoring
includes.description: External data sources and pipelines are monitored as operational dependencies of deployed ML systems.

includes.label: Prediction and candidate-output persistence
includes.description: Persist production inputs, live predictions, and shadow candidate predictions for later monitoring and comparison.

selected_clusters.name: Model Governance and Accountability
selected_clusters.description: How are regulatory alignment, monitoring ownership, and long-term accountability established?

values.label: Regulatory and business alignment
values.description: MLOps practices align deployed models with organizational needs and regulatory requirements.

selected_clusters.name: Model Adoption and Value Realization
selected_clusters.description: Documents vary in how organizations move models from experiments into sustained use through transparency, stakeholder engagement, collaboration, and demonstrated value.

values.label: Operational value realization
values.description: Models are moved into operational use to solve business problems and generate measurable value. The emphasis is on deployment and sustained use rather than on broader adoption practices.

includes.label: Production use for value realization
includes.description: Models create meaningful value only when deployed and actually used in operational settings.

selected_clusters.name: ML Asset Versioning
selected_clusters.description: Which ML code, data, and model artifacts are versioned and retained for reproducibility?

values.label: Comprehensive ML artifact versioning
values.description: Source code, datasets, models, schemas, executables, and dependencies are versioned and retained through version-control and artifact-management systems to support reproducibility.

includes.label: Versioned ML artifacts
includes.description: Source code, data, models, schemas, executables, and dependencies are managed through version control and artifact repositories.

includes.label: Source-controlled ML pipeline code
includes.description: Pipeline and application source code is stored in version-controlled repositories for collaboration and delivery.

selected_clusters.name: ML Architecture Governance
selected_clusters.description: How are ML solution architecture and process standards defined, reviewed, and traced?

values.label: Predefined architecture and process framework
values.description: A predefined framework guides architectural decisions and systematic treatment of non-functional requirements.

selected_clusters.name: Model Family and Objective Selection
selected_clusters.description: Which model family, ensemble approach, or prioritized objective guides model selection?

relations.reading: Choices on Model Family and Objective Selection affect the outcomes of Model Packaging Format
relations.rationale: Model complexity and optimization choices influence deployability and serving requirements.

values.label: Automated model-family selection
values.description: AutoML selects among alternative model families as part of pipeline construction.

values.label: Model ensembling
values.description: Multiple models are combined to improve predictive stability or score.

values.label: Explicit model-objective prioritization
values.description: Teams choose which quality objective, such as false-negative minimization, to optimize.

selected_clusters.name: Hyperparameter and Architecture Optimization
selected_clusters.description: How are hyperparameters and model architectures searched, tuned, and evaluated for practical deployment?

values.label: Manual hyperparameter tuning
values.description: Practitioners tune model hyperparameters by hand and trial and error for smaller modeling tasks.

values.label: Automated hyperparameter optimization
values.description: Search procedures automatically optimize model hyperparameters when manual exploration is impractical.

selected_clusters.name: ML Execution Caching and Resumption
selected_clusters.description: Which mechanisms cache, retain, and resume intermediate ML execution state?

values.label: Application-managed persistent caching
values.description: Applications explicitly persist reusable computation results in files, buckets, or databases.

values.label: ElastiCache model state
values.description: Current model parameters and inference features are retrieved from an in-memory store.

selected_clusters.name: ML Metadata, Metrics, and Artifact Tracking
selected_clusters.description: Which mechanisms record ML metadata, metrics, and versioned artifacts for reproducibility and operations?

values.label: Comprehensive pipeline lifecycle tracking
values.description: A metadata-backed system captures pipeline executions, metrics, experiments, lineage, parameters, and versioned artifacts across the ML lifecycle.

includes.label: ML metadata store
includes.description: A metadata store records pipeline executions, parameters, metrics, lineage, and comparison context.

includes.label: Training and testing metric recording
includes.description: Training and test metrics are retained to compare newly trained and previous models.

includes.label: Pipeline execution metadata capture
includes.description: Capture execution timing, parameters, and run metadata for pipeline and experiment tracking.

includes.label: Version-controlled data and model artifacts
includes.description: Data inputs, generated models, and pipeline artifacts are versioned for reproducibility.

includes.label: Experiment and training-run tracking
includes.description: Experiments and training runs are recorded and organized to compare models and support reproducibility.

selected_clusters.name: Online Model Update Strategy
selected_clusters.description: Which learning and parameter-update approach adapts models to incoming data while supporting prediction serving?

relations.reading: Choices on Online Model Update Strategy affect the outcomes of Production Model Monitoring
relations.rationale: Incremental updates, persistence, and atomicity determine what drift, staleness, and consistency signals monitoring must observe.

values.label: Incremental linear learning
values.description: Linear or logistic learners update rapidly from incoming examples for online learning.

values.label: Periodic model-parameter persistence
values.description: Learned parameters are periodically persisted so real-time prediction workers can use current model state.

selected_clusters.name: Data Processing Mode
selected_clusters.description: Which temporal execution mode processes data for training, feature generation, or prediction?

relations.reading: Choices on Data Processing Mode limit the options available on Feature Computation Timing
relations.rationale: Batch, real-time, near-real-time, and streaming modes constrain whether features are precomputed, asynchronous, or request-time.

values.label: Batch processing
values.description: Process data as discrete jobs or recurring offline runs.

values.label: Real-time processing
values.description: Process data continuously with minimal delay while it moves through the pipeline.

values.label: Offline versus real-time execution placement
values.description: Risk workloads execute offline or in real time according to urgency and computational requirements.
